h1:
Where to Stay in Bueng Kan?
12 Hotels We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Twelve Bueng Kan hotels across every budget — a garden-bungalow resort and a lakefront boutique minutes from Naka Cave, an in-town hotel with a waterslide pool, down to a Thai-house guesthouse from ฿600. Covering the city centre, Bueng Khong Long lakeside, the Phu Tok side and the Mekong riverfront. Starting from around ฿450–1,800/night.
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right base in Bueng Kan matter?
introHtml: Bueng Kan is Thailand's smallest and newest province, and its headline sights — Naka Cave, Three Whale Rock, Phu Tok and Bueng Khong Long lake — are scattered across different corners and a fair drive from the town. Many people book without checking the location, then spend hours each day driving tens of kilometres just to reach the sights. This guide rounds up 12 Bueng Kan hotels we've picked and reviewed across every tier — from a garden-bungalow resort and a lakefront boutique near Naka Cave, to an in-town hotel with a pool and full facilities, down to a budget guesthouse run by its owner — each with an honest take from real reviews, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Bueng Kan has no metro and limited public transport within the province — having your own car or a rental is the key, because the sights sit far from town. The main areas in this guide: Bueng Kan city centre — by Lotus, the Mekong riverfront and the Thai–Lao market, easy for food and shopping (The One, B2, BK Place, The Wisdom, Century Grand, M Grand) · Bueng Khong Long — on the lake and closest to Naka Cave and Phu Langka (HR Resort, Lake House, Movit, Thai Guest House) · Near Phu Tok (Non Sombun) — garden bungalows, an easy start toward Phu Tok (Surocha) · The Mekong riverfront (Pak Khat) — river views and sunsets, on the Nong Khai–Bueng Kan route (Khong Khamkun).

entries.name: HR Resort Bueng Khong Long
entries.revCount: 180 reviews · highest score in this list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bueng Khong Long · 15-min drive to Naka Cave
entries.addr: 98/1 Ban Non Champa, Bueng Khong Long, Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this list at 9.2 from 180 reviews — HR Resort is a garden bungalow resort in Bueng Khong Long, the closest stay to Naka Cave in this group, about 15 minutes' drive from the Naka Cave trailhead. Guests consistently praise the quiet, airy feel, the privacy of detached wooden bungalows, and rooms that look clean and fresh. The real standout is breakfast — à la carte Thai and continental with fresh coffee — and an owner who welcomes you like a houseguest. Best for couples and families who've driven in for Naka Cave and want to genuinely unwind.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There are only about 8 bungalows and they fill fast around Naka Cave season — book ahead, and ask the owner about the route and timing for Naka Cave at check-in to plan the next day.
pros: Highest score in the list, 9.2 from 180 reviews
Wooden bungalows in a garden, quiet, private, fresh-looking rooms
À la carte breakfast and fresh coffee widely praised
Near Naka Cave and Bueng Khong Long lake, owner-run
cons: Rural location — you need a car, nothing within walking distance
No in-room work desk; some nights carry noise from nearby events

entries.name: The One Hotel Bueng Kan
entries.badge: 🛝 In town with a waterslide pool
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Rd · next to Lotus
entries.addr: 459 Moo 1, Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Rd, Mueang Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: The One Hotel is one of the top in-town hotels in Bueng Kan and ranked #1 of 5 town hotels on TripAdvisor, scoring 9.1 from 58 reviews. It opened in 2010 and had a major refurbishment in 2022, sitting on Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Road right by Lotus. What sets it apart from a typical city hotel is the outdoor pool with a waterslide and a separate kids' pool, which families love. There's a gym, a cooked-to-order buffet breakfast, free parking and an EV charger that's rare in this province.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Room condition varies, so ask for a refurbished room when booking or at check-in. If you have kids, leave time in the early evening for the waterslide pool — it's their favourite part.
pros: #1 in-town hotel on TripAdvisor, score 9.1
Pool with a waterslide and a kids' pool, great for families
Next to Lotus, free parking and an EV charger
Rooms larger than the price suggests; English-speaking staff
cons: Listed as 4-star on some sites but really a solid city hotel
Some beds are firm; in-room amenities occasionally incomplete

entries.name: B2 Bueng Kan Boutique & Budget
entries.revCount: 263 reviews · most reviews in this list
entries.addr: 811 Moo 7, Chayangkun Rd, Wisit, Mueang Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: B2 Bueng Kan is a 2024 new-build with the most reviews in this list — 263 — and a 9.0 score, which is high for a budget hotel. Part of the B2 chain, it sits on Chayangkun Road in central Bueng Kan, near the Mekong riverfront and the Thai–Lao market. What guests like most is that it's a new building with fresh, clean rooms in a simple modern style, with smart TVs and fast Wi-Fi. There's a lift, free parking and 24-hour reception — handy for anyone using Bueng Kan as a driving base.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Sound insulation isn't great, so ask for a higher floor or a room away from the main corridor. Screenshot your booked rate too — a few reviewers found the check-in price didn't match the booking.
pros: Most reviews in the list, 263, score 9.0
2024 new build, clean rooms, modern design
Central location, near the river and the Thai–Lao market
Free Wi-Fi and parking, lift, 24-hr reception
cons: No pool or gym; sound insulation isn't great
Some rooms lack a hairdryer; some bathrooms drain slowly

entries.name: Lake House Naka Cave
entries.revCount: 89 reviews · every room a lake view
entries.badge: 🏞️ On the lake, all lake-view rooms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On Bueng Khong Long · near Naka Cave
entries.addr: 220 Ban Non Sawan, Bueng Khong Long, Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: Lake House Naka Cave is a white minimalist boutique on Bueng Khong Long where every room faces the lake. It opened in early 2023 and scores 9.0 from 89 reviews — two white buildings, 10 rooms, right on the lakeshore. The draw is that every room has a private balcony overlooking water and hills, so you wake to the lake, with breakfast served in a zone that looks out over it. Best for couples, small families and pilgrims visiting Naka Cave who want a riverside-style stay with a view, rather than a fully-equipped city hotel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for the Deluxe King Lake View for the fullest lake view. With only 10 rooms it fills fast, so book ahead, bring insect spray for the balcony at dusk, and wake early for the morning mist over the lake.
pros: Every room a Bueng Khong Long view, with a private balcony
Clean, minimalist rooms; breakfast included with a lake view
Quiet, restful riverside setting near Naka Cave
Attentive service, high review scores
cons: A small 10-room boutique selling the view, not a full-service city hotel
Insects at dusk as at any waterside stay; the access road is steep

entries.name: Movit Nakathibodi Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On Bueng Khong Long · 15 min to Naka Cave
entries.addr: 499 Moo 12, Bueng Khong Long, Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: Movit Nakathibodi Resort is a budget-friendly lakefront resort of white-and-wood Japanese-style detached houses on Bueng Khong Long, scoring 8.8 from 51 reviews and a former Travellers' Choice. The signature is the Japanese-house design set in nature, with balconies over the garden and lake and a small on-site café for coffee with a view. It sits in Bueng Khong Long town — walk 200–300 m to the market, 7-Eleven and Cafe Amazon — and it's only 8 km to Naka Cave.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a house facing the lake for the fullest view, and test the water heater when you arrive — if it's not right, staff will move you. Sit at the café early to catch the morning mist over the lake.
pros: Japanese-style houses on Bueng Khong Long with lovely lake views
Great value for the setting; on-site café
Walk to the market, hospital and convenience stores
Only a 15-minute drive to Naka Cave; helpful staff
cons: A small resort; maintenance in places needs ongoing attention
Water heater issues in some rooms; insects at the water's edge at dusk

entries.name: Thai Guest House Bung Khong Long
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bueng Khong Long · walk to the market
tags: 🛒 Walk to Bueng Khong Long market
entries.addr: 195/2 Moo 12, Bueng Khong Long, Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: Thai Guest House is a Thai-house guesthouse in a garden, owner-run, with rooms from a few hundred baht, scoring 8.7 from 120 reviews. It's a small place — about 10 rooms across two houses — in the community, within walking distance of Bueng Khong Long's market and park. What lifts its score is the warm, family-style hospitality, help with Naka Cave routes, and local-style breakfast included for two. Rooms have air-con, fridge and TV and are clean beyond the price. Ideal for budget travellers visiting Naka Cave.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for Thai House 2 if you want a newer room, or Thai House 1 for the cheapest rate. Rooms are limited and fill fast in festival season, so book ahead — and ask the owner about chartering a car up to Naka Cave at check-in.
pros: Under ฿1,000 including breakfast for two — great value
Owner and team are warm, like staying with relatives
Clean rooms with air-con, fridge and TV for the price
Walk to Bueng Khong Long market; a good Naka Cave base
cons: Rooms and décor are simple, in line with guesthouse pricing
Not on Naka Cave or the lake — a further 7–8 km drive

entries.name: BK Place Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In town · on Highway 222 · 5 min to the river
entries.addr: 168 Moo 9, Bueng Kan–Phang Khon Rd, on Highway 222, Mueang Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: BK Place Hotel is a city hotel selling big rooms, easy parking and low rates from just ฿450, scoring 8.6. It opened in 2014 on Bueng Kan–Phang Khon Road by Highway 222, about a 5-minute drive to the river and town. Deluxe rooms at around 32 sqm are spacious, some with a tub and a balcony. There's a pool and a small kids' water park with a slide, plus the Krau BK restaurant. Good for families and self-drivers using Bueng Kan as a base for Phu Tok, Naka Cave or Bueng Khong Long.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Deluxe costs little more than a Standard but is noticeably bigger — good value. Ask for a room away from the water-park side to avoid afternoon-to-evening noise, and reserve breakfast at check-in (not included, about ฿100/person).
pros: Big rooms, large beds, low rates from ฿450
Pool and a kids' water park, great for families with children
Wide parking on Highway 222, easy to drive on from
On-site restaurant; helpful staff
cons: Rooms and furniture are ageing; very few reviews so far
Water park is noisy in the afternoon; breakfast not included

entries.name: The Wisdom Residence
entries.revCount: 218 reviews · new rooms, walk to Lotus
entries.addr: 503 Moo 1, Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Rd, Wisit, Mueang Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: The Wisdom Residence is an apart-hotel-style stay with fresh, clean rooms and plenty of reviews — 218 in all — scoring 8.4. It's on Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Road in town, about 26 rooms, many with balconies. Guests like the relatively new rooms, the large fridge and free daily drinking water, and a location a few minutes' walk from Lotus and 7-Eleven. Crucially, reception arranges transport to Naka Cave, Three Whale Rock and Phu Tok — handy if you didn't drive in.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's no lift, so ask for an upper-floor room with a balcony for a better view and more privacy than the ground-floor rooms facing the car park. If you didn't drive, tell reception in advance to arrange transport to the sights.
pros: New, clean rooms with balconies, a big fridge and free water
In-town location, a walk to Lotus and 7-Eleven, low rates
Reception arranges cars to Naka Cave, Three Whale Rock, Phu Tok
Lots of reviews (218); free parking
cons: No lift — upper-floor rooms mean stairs
No pool; Wi-Fi is sometimes weak

entries.name: Surocha Resort (near Phu Tok)
tags: 🚗 Base for Phu Tok & Naka Cave
entries.addr: 168 Moo 1, Non Sombun, Mueang Bueng Kan (Bueng Kan–Phon Thong Rd, km 8)
entries.storyHtml: Surocha Resort is a resort of detached bungalows in a large garden, a base for driving to Phu Tok and Naka Cave, scoring 8.0 from 18 reviews. It's in Non Sombun on Bueng Kan–Phon Thong Road, about 8–9 km from town. Guests note the spacious rooms, the leafy, quiet grounds, and parking right at your door, with some two-room units for families. There's a restaurant, karaoke and a function room. Good for self-drive travellers who want plenty of space at a low rate, fanning out to Phu Tok, Phu Langka and Three Whale Rock.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a group, ask about the two-room bungalow — bigger and better value. Standard rooms don't include breakfast, so pick up something in town first, and start early for Phu Tok (about 40 km away).
pros: Bungalows in a large garden, quiet, with spacious rooms
A base for Phu Tok, Phu Langka and Naka Cave in every direction
Low rates, lots of space, park at your door
Two-room units suit families and groups
cons: Simple upcountry-resort rooms; breakfast not included
Outside town — you need a car; still few reviews

entries.name: Century Grand Hotel
entries.revCount: 403 reviews · big rooms, lots of parking
entries.addr: 180 Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Rd, Moo 8, Mueang Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: Century Grand Hotel is a city hotel selling big rooms, easy parking and a light price — and it has the most reviews in this list at 403, scoring 7.0. It opened around 2012, with 80 rooms on Bueng Kan–Nakhon Phanom Road near Tesco Lotus and Makro. The talking points are rooms that feel large for the price, comfortable big beds and a large bathroom, plus plenty of parking front and back. Staff are friendly — one review mentions a lift to the bus station. Good for self-drive travellers wanting a value base, not atmosphere or views.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel is about 10 years old and some furniture is dated — ask to see the room before check-in if you can, and pick a higher, recently-refreshed floor; some upper rooms even get a hill and town view.
pros: The most reviews in this list, 403
Big rooms, comfortable large beds, large bathrooms
Plenty of free parking, near Tesco Lotus and Makro
Friendly staff; affordable rates
cons: An older hotel; ageing furniture and inconsistent cleanliness
About 1–2 km from the river and the town centre

entries.name: M Grand Hotel
entries.addr: 159 Moo 10, Non Sombun, Mueang Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: M Grand Hotel is a budget city hotel with roomy spaces and easy parking, scoring 7.0 from 32 reviews. It's a small place of about 30 rooms in Non Sombun, within the Bueng Kan town area. Reviewers note rooms larger than expected for the price, a quiet feel, and free parking — important in a province where you rely on your own car. There's free Wi-Fi, free bikes to borrow around town and a Thai massage service. Good for self-drive travellers or a stopover before Phu Tok and Naka Cave.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Room quality is uneven — ask to see the room before check-in if you can and pick a recently-cleaned one. Groups should choose the Family Room for better value, and start early for Phu Tok (about 18 km away).
pros: Budget rate, larger rooms than expected, quiet feel
Free, easy parking — good for self-drive travellers
Free bikes to borrow and a Thai massage service
Works as a base before Phu Tok and Naka Cave
cons: Some rooms look dated; cleanliness is inconsistent
No pool; limited in-house food options

entries.name: Khong Khamkun Hotel (riverside)
entries.revCount: few reviews · sells the Mekong view
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mekong riverfront · Pak Khat · ~40 km from town
entries.addr: 62 Moo 6, Ban Tha Na Khun, Pak Khat, Bueng Kan
entries.storyHtml: Khong Khamkun Hotel is a Mekong-riverfront boutique at Pak Khat that sells the sunset-over-the-river view. It's a 21-room boutique that opened around 2020, facing the Mekong, about 40 km from Bueng Kan town on the Nong Khai–Bueng Kan route. The real draw is the riverside setting — many rooms and the restaurant look out over the water to Laos, with a pool and a riverside lobby bar. Honestly, reviews are still few and the score isn't settled, and rooms are simple and a bit dated — best for self-drive travellers along the Mekong who value the river view above all.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: When booking, specifically ask for a room facing the Mekong, since the view is the whole reason to stay. Arrive before evening to catch the sunset, and bring your own car — there's little around Pak Khat.
pros: Mekong view and sunset are the highlight
Quiet by the river; a pool and a riverside restaurant
Budget rate, wide parking, friendly staff
A good overnight stop on a Mekong road trip
cons: Rooms and furniture are simple and dated; pool upkeep is inconsistent
Far from Bueng Kan town — you need a car; still few reviews

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate and may change by date and season — always check the live rate and compare 3 sites before booking. In Bueng Kan the sights are spread far from town, so having your own car or a rental matters a lot. Around Naka Cave season (especially after Phu Langka National Park opens) and on long weekends, Bueng Khong Long stays fill fast and prices rise — book 1–2 months ahead. Around the end of Buddhist Lent, people gather on the Mekong for the Naga fireballs. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Bueng Kan hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in for Bueng Kan?
faq.a: It depends on your main goal. Bueng Khong Long is best for Naka Cave, Phu Langka and Bueng Khong Long lake, as it's closest to the sights (HR Resort, Lake House, Movit, Thai Guest House). Bueng Kan city centre suits travellers who want food and shops, near Lotus, the river and the Thai–Lao market, and a base for several directions (The One, B2, BK Place, The Wisdom, Century Grand). Near Phu Tok (Non Sombun) suits Phu Tok-focused trips (Surocha, M Grand). The Mekong riverfront (Pak Khat) suits Mekong road-trippers who want a river view (Khong Khamkun).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Bueng Kan hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary but are generally lighter than big tourist provinces: budget city hotels and guesthouses start around ฿450–730 a night; resorts and lakeside stays on Bueng Khong Long run about ฿900–1,100; an in-town hotel with a pool and full facilities is around ฿1,100; and a lakefront boutique with view rooms starts around ฿1,800. Around Naka Cave season and long weekends, Bueng Khong Long stays cost more and fill quickly.

faq.q: ❓ Which Bueng Kan stay is closest to Naka Cave?
faq.a: Stays in Bueng Khong Long are closest to Naka Cave (Phu Langka National Park). HR Resort is about a 15-minute drive to the trailhead; Movit Nakathibodi Resort is about 8 km (15 minutes); Lake House Naka Cave is on the lake, about 40–60 minutes' drive; Thai Guest House is a walk to the Bueng Khong Long market, then a further 7–8 km drive. Compared with hotels in Bueng Kan town, which sit about an hour from Naka Cave, the Bueng Khong Long area is far more convenient if Naka Cave is the focus.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a car for Bueng Kan?
faq.a: Very much so. Bueng Kan is a small province with limited public transport, and headline sights like Naka Cave, Three Whale Rock and Phu Tok are 30 km to over an hour's drive from town. Most people self-drive or rent. If you don't have a car, choose a stay where reception can arrange transport (such as The Wisdom Residence) or a guesthouse where the owner helps charter a car (such as Thai Guest House or HR Resort).

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Bueng Kan hotel?
faq.a: For ordinary weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is fine. But around Naka Cave season (after Phu Langka National Park opens) and on long weekends, the small Bueng Khong Long stays (HR Resort with about 8 bungalows, Lake House with 10 rooms) fill very fast — book 1–2 months ahead. Around the end of Buddhist Lent, when people come to watch the Naga fireballs on the Mekong, riverside rooms also fill quickly.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking a Bueng Kan hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so it's worth comparing all three before you book. Every review page in this guide includes price-comparison links across all three — it can save you a few hundred baht a night.
